title: Choose the visual world for althologram
question: The roll assigned the Showcard Marquee. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Showcard Marquee
options.lineage: Fairground attraction banners and chaser-bulb theatre marquees, 1920s–60s
options.thesis: The fan is the attraction; the page is the painted banner and bulb marquee that make a crowd stop at the door.
options.viewport: One vermilion painted banner edge to edge. Across the top, a brass marquee strip with chaser bulbs carries the name and the nav. Left, the showcard headline in heavy outlined lettering: SEE IT FLOAT, then one line of plain copy. Right, a bulb-framed attraction window, black inside, playing a real hologram clip of a bottle spinning in mid-air. Under it a painted ADMISSION board: Fan + cover $250, Content $150, Tripod $99, each a tick-box, and a ticket-booth button, Request a quote, with the running total on it. Below the banner the page continues as the next painted panel: the fan running in a real wine aisle.
options.risk: Kitsch if the lettering is drawn like clipart or the bulbs become a glow effect; it has to be set like a 1940s showcard writer would, with real black inside the frames only.

raised.raise: One light source: every highlight on the page is tungsten from the marquee bulbs, so the black attraction windows are the only place colour glows.
Banded ledger rhythm: the whole page is stacked painted panels of fixed height, no floating card grid anywhere.
Every panel carries a painted placard code (No. 1 THE FAN, No. 2 THE CONTENT…) so a visitor always knows which attraction they are reading.
One continuous banner, one scroll pass: sections are the next panel of the same cloth, never a new page style.
Specs are instruments with units painted on dials, never a badge row.

options.label: Gold Leaf on the Window
options.lineage: Sign-painters’ gilded shop-window lettering, read from the street at night
options.thesis: The page is the shop’s own window: gold-leaf lettering on glass, and behind the glass the fan is already running.
options.viewport: Dark shop interior seen through the window. Gold-leaf lettering across the glass carries the headline and the three prices; the fan floats a hologram clip inside the dark room behind it; the quote form sits on the door panel, with the reversed OPEN sign.
options.risk: Familiar: artisanal gold-leaf signage is where many craft brands and most runs in this category land. Reads vintage if the glass is not convincingly dark and real behind the letters.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.lineage: Metropolitan rail diagrams fired as enamel murals
options.thesis: Buying is a journey on one scarlet line: Fan, Cover, Content, Tripod, Installed, with the places it runs as stations.
options.viewport: A midnight enamel panel with the offer drawn as a route diagram: four stations with prices on a scarlet line, a cobalt branch for the places (bar, café, window, booth), and the quote form as the journey planner at the interchange.
options.case: Everyone reads a transit map, and prices as stations are clear; it loses on proof, because a diagram never shows the picture floating.
options.risk: The floating image, the whole argument, becomes a thumbnail at a station.

options.label: Indoor Weather Sun
options.lineage: A monofrequency sun in a hazed hall under a mirrored ceiling
options.thesis: The shop as a hall, the fan as the sun, everything flattened to amber.
options.viewport: A vast amber hall with the fan as the half sun on the far wall.
options.case: Shop owners do not identify with an art installation, and amber monochrome kills the colour clips that prove the product.
options.kept: One light source governs every highlight.

options.label: Jacquard Punched Brocade
options.lineage: Punch-card looms weaving gold on midnight silk
options.thesis: The picture as thousands of binary LED choices, woven row by row.
options.viewport: A loom sequence of punch-card rows resolving into the logo.
options.case: The mechanism analogy is real, but a liquor-store owner reads brocade as fashion, not signage.
options.kept: Banded ledger rhythm with no floating cards.

options.label: Starship Crew Terminal
options.lineage: Used-future green phosphor terminals with hazard plates
options.thesis: Specs typed out line by line on curved glass.
options.viewport: A typed readout of the offer under striped hazard plates.
options.case: Sci-fi nostalgia, not a shop owner’s world, and black-with-glow is the category rut this version exists to leave.
options.kept: Every zone carries a painted placard code.

options.label: Ebru Floated Pigment
options.lineage: Pigment combed on a water bath and lifted once onto paper
options.thesis: The page as one liquid surface the visitor combs.
options.viewport: A marbled bath that redistributes as you move.
options.case: Beautiful and unreadable; neither the buyer nor the offer survives it.
options.kept: One continuous surface, one scroll pass.

options.label: Night-Flight Six-Pack
options.lineage: A small aircraft’s six luminous instruments
options.thesis: Six specs as six dials on a matte black panel.
options.viewport: A gauge cluster for rpm, diameter, LEDs, pixels, watts, angle.
options.case: Specs become legible, but a gauge cluster never says a picture floats in your window, and shop owners are not pilots.
options.kept: Numbers are instruments with units, never badges.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark hologram-tech landing page every fan seller ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Centered headline over a glowing render of the fan, a primary button, then three equal offer cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
